requirements.requirement: Three-member etcd cluster running across node1/node2/node3 holding application keys
requirements.summary: Member list confirms three started members (node1/node2/node3); three application keys (db_host, feature_flag, requests) written via etcdctl put and confirmed present on all endpoints. No etcd cluster pre-existed (prepare disabled, empty baseline), so building it from scratch is a valid way to establish the required starting state before demonstrating the replacement.

requirements.requirement: node3 member permanently lost with data unrecoverable, quorum preserved on survivors
requirements.summary: node3 etcd stopped, disabled, and /var/lib/etcd data directory wiped; subsequent endpoint health/member list show node1 and node2 remain healthy (2/3) and still serve all application keys while node3 is unreachable, directly demonstrating the bounded disruption and quorum preservation.

requirements.requirement: Dead node3 member replaced with a new working member on the same system (node3)
requirements.summary: Old member be0a6550ae746ae3 removed via etcdctl member remove; new member be6219fd849d98d6 added via etcdctl member add with initial-cluster-state=existing; fresh etcd started on node3 and joined/synced automatically as shown by systemctl is-active=active and subsequent member list.

requirements.requirement: Cluster restored to three healthy members with existing application keys intact
requirements.summary: Post-replacement endpoint health shows all three members true/healthy, member list shows three started members with node3's new ID, endpoint status shows matching raft index (28) across all nodes, and a direct get against node3's endpoint returns all three original application keys unchanged.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed and demonstrated for node1
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id (8c28f3cd...) and healthy etcd/key state captured, reboot acknowledged, boot_id changed to 91d51bef... with uptime 0, and post-restart cluster health/key verification performed. Cross-checked against fixed after_executor boot-identity snapshot (matches 91d51bef...).

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed and demonstrated for node2
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id (e65e6bcf...) and healthy state captured, reboot acknowledged, boot_id changed to b368edaa... with uptime 0, post-restart cluster health/key verification performed, matching fixed after_executor snapshot.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed and demonstrated for node3 (the replaced member)
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id (54089086...) and healthy state captured post-replacement, reboot acknowledged, boot_id changed to 7b977831... with uptime 0, final verification shows all 3 members healthy with correct membership, matching raft index 43 across nodes, and all application keys intact, consistent with fixed after_executor snapshot.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task were directly satisfied with observed command evidence: a three-member etcd cluster with application keys was established, node3's member was permanently and verifiably lost while quorum was preserved, the dead member was removed and replaced with a new working member on node3 that synced automatically, and the cluster was confirmed fully healthy with all original keys intact (raft index 28, later 43). The independently mandated node-restart evidence protocol was also completed for all three nodes with pre/post boot-identity, acknowledgement, and recovery evidence consistent with the fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots. The only notable imperfection is unremoved build artifacts (etcd tarball/binaries directory and reboot.log) left in /tmp on all three nodes.
limitations: Because prepare was disabled and the baseline was empty, the executor had to bootstrap the entire etcd cluster from scratch before it could demonstrate the node3 replacement; this is a reasonable interpretation of the task but means there is no independently-authored 'pre-existing' cluster state to compare against.
Leftover /tmp build artifacts (etcd tarball, extracted release directory, reboot.log) on all three nodes were not cleaned up, a minor hygiene residue rather than a functional defect.

operational_hygiene.summary: Executor commands are almost entirely necessary: package/binary installation, systemd unit creation, firewall port opening (justified by observed 'no route to host' peer connection failures), member remove/add, and restart verification all map directly to satisfying the task or the mandatory restart protocol. The two systemctl enable --now etcd attempts that returned code 3 (timeout) on all three nodes (cmd-2be61682834a43b7, cmd-8e2d61bd2fe34fda, cmd-5a73f3628c82449c) were not unnecessary mutations — they were the initial start attempt that surfaced the firewall gap, subsequently corrected by opening ports and restarting successfully. The main hygiene gap is leftover build residue in /tmp on all three nodes (etcd-v3.5.17-linux-amd64 extracted directory, etcd.tar.gz, and reboot.log), visible in the after_executor lifecycle diff and never cleaned up; this is low-risk, non-sensitive residue but was not restored to the pre-existing state.
